title: Renewal triggers, SLA translation, and KPI ledger
content:
Purpose and audience:
- Purpose: create a single, practical ledger that translates infra/signal metrics (latency, uptime, cost/token, cache-hit) into renewal signals and QBR talking points; provide sample KPI table templates and an action runbook for trigger responses.
- Audience: CSMs owning mid-market and enterprise renewals, CS engineering liaisons, and Growth AEs prepping QBRs.

Summary / Quick read (TL;DR):
- Define canonical measurement windows and aggregation for four signals: P50/P95 latency (api), customer-level uptime, cost per 1k tokens, and prefix cache-hit rate.
- Provide numeric thresholds for low/medium/high risk buckets and human-friendly translations for QBR decks.
- Include sample ledger for three accounts and a short runbook with owners and SLA for first-touch and escalation.

Metric definitions (canonical):
1) Latency (api_request_latency_ms)
   - What: end-to-end server-side request latency measured server receive -> first byte emitted (ms). Excludes client network.
   - Window: rolling 7d and 30d. Present both P50 and P95.
   - Aggregation: compute percentiles on per-request latencies per-customer per-model-route; then report percentiles.
   - Formula / note: P95 is the 95th percentile across all requests in window; prefer P95 for production SLO conversation.

2) Uptime (route_success_rate)
   - What: proportion of requests that returned 200-level responses within SLO time (default 10s)
   - Window: rolling 30d, daily granularity for trend.
   - Aggregation: successful_requests / total_requests. Non-retriable 5xx counts as failure.
   - SLO mapping: 99.95% -> gold, 99.9% -> standard, below 99.5% -> at-risk.

3) Cost per token (cost_per_1k_tokens_usd)
   - What: estimated spend for a customer per 1,000 output+input tokens (billing tokens), normalized to USD. Uses model variant pricing + amortized infra overhead.
   - Window: monthly rolling (30d). Show median and 90th percentile of per-request cost.
   - Notes: includes caching credit (see cache-hit below) and burst premium if on dedicated.

4) Cache-hit rate (prefix_cache_hit_pct)
   - What: fraction of requests that were served from prefix or KV cache (no generation tokens billed) for identical prefixes.
   - Window: rolling 7d and 30d.
   - Aggregation: cache_hits / eligible_requests (requests with prefix eligibility flag set).
   - Note: distinguish prefix cache vs response cache; this ledger focuses on prefix/KV caching.

Risk bucket thresholds (guideline — tune per-account):
- Latency (P95):
  - Green: <= 450ms P95 (7d); Amber: 450ms < P95 <= 1200ms; Red: P95 > 1200ms or sustained increase >50% vs prior 30d.
- Uptime (30d):
  - Green: >= 99.95%; Amber: 99.5% - 99.95%; Red: < 99.5% or repeated daily dips >0.5%.
- Cost/1k tokens (USD):
  - Green: within 15% of expected contract benchmark; Amber: 15-40% over; Red: >40% over or unexplained spikes.
- Cache-hit rate (30d):
  - Green: >= 25% (for prefix-eligible workloads); Amber: 10-25%; Red: <10% or downward trend >30% vs prior 30d.

Notes on combining signals into renewal trigger:
- Single red in uptime -> immediate escalation (high severity).
- Latency red + cost amber -> operational playbook (improve batching/quantization, check routing policies).
- Cache-hit red with cost red -> product ops + SE engagement to enable prefix caching or caching rules.
- Persistent amber across two metrics for 30+ days -> flag for QBR renewal risk talking points and potential commercial levers.

Sample KPI ledger (table-ready rows) — paste into QBR slide: (columns: account, seg, window, p95_ms, uptime_pct, cost_per_1k_usd, cache_hit_pct, risk_level, note)
- Acme Retail, enterprise, 30d, 760, 99.92, 2.10, 12, MEDIUM, "P95 latency amber; cost slightly high due to small batches; SE suggested batching config"
- BrightHealth, mid-market, 30d, 320, 99.98, 0.95, 34, LOW, "Great cache adoption; consider committed capacity upsell"
- NovaChat, startup, 30d, 1600, 99.40, 2.85, 6, HIGH, "Multiple outages and cache drop-offs; CS/SE on site; renewals at risk"

Playbook: first 48 hours (triage -> action -> escalate)
- Triage (first 2 hours): CSM/engineer quick assessment; owner = assigned CSM; artifact: open Jira CS- triage ticket with metric snapshots and runbook template.
- Action (2-24 hours): If uptime red: open incident with SRE + notify customer; if latency red: propose immediate policy changes (route to faster region or switch model variant) and test config in staging; if cost spike: run request-sample analysis to isolate cause (prompt changes, model shift, traffic pattern).
- Escalate (24-48 hours): If issue not resolved or customer unhappy, escalate to CS director + Solutions Eng leader; prepare one-pager for exec QBR with remediation plan and ask (credits, committed capacity, or engineering SLA).
- Owners and SLAs in practice: CSM 2h triage, CS-Engineer 8h deep-dive, SE/SRE 24h mitigation plan, CS Director 48h executive brief.

QBR talking points mapping (humanize metrics):
- Latency: "Customers saw P95 experience of 760ms over the last month, 1.7x higher than last quarter due to smaller batch sizes during peak hours. Recommended immediate mitigation: increase batch size for route 'chat.v1'."
- Uptime: "Overall uptime 99.92% (30d). There were 3 short incidents in week 42; we deployed a routing fallback which reduced impact. Ask: Do you want an SLA add-on for 99.99%?"
- Cost: "Effective cost per 1k tokens is $2.10, which is 22% above expectation driven by long-context generation. Suggest: enable 8-bit quantization profile and enable prefix caching to reduce repeated tokens."
- Cache: "Cache hit is 12% (30d); enabling prefix caching for the 5 highest-volume prefixes should yield ~25% token savings. SE can run a 2-week pilot."

Template checklist for QBR prep (CSM):
- Pull 30d and 7d metric snapshots for the account (latency P50/P95, uptime rolling, cost per 1k, cache-hit) 
- Annotate any config changes, model swaps, or product releases during the window 
- Fill the one-page KPI ledger row and attach sample request traces for any anomalies 
- Decide ask for the customer (credits, committed capacity, SE time, SLA) and prep slides with recommended actions and estimated upside

Open questions / TODOs (notes-to-self):
- Should we standardize the window for cost to calendar month only? Ops needs alignment with billing.
- Need a lightweight dashboard widget that shows latency delta vs baseline for each account (spike detection). Chase product metrics team (PRD req id?).
- Validate cache-hit definition with infra team: do we include partial-KV hits or only full-prefix short-circuits?

Appendix: sample Jira template (copy into ticket):
- Title: [CS Triage] <account> - <metric> - <short summary>
- Fields: customer, CSM, severity, metric snapshots (7d/30d), sample request ids, initial hypothesis, immediate mitigations attempted
- Expected SLA for comment: SRE to acknowledge within 1 hour for uptime-red incidents.

Authors & provenance:
- Drafted by Aisha Kumar (CSM), pulled metric definitions from Confluence metric library, engineering verification by Liam Chen (CS-Engineer) and Priya Nair (Solutions Eng).

Notes: this is intentionally practical and slightly informal — copy the ledger rows into client-ready slides but keep the playbook in internal docs. Mark final after engineering confirms cache definition and product signs off on cost model.
